From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finova.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finova.com
Date: 2026-05-22T15:04:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff + perf eval template

Ben — thanks, receiving MAP template. We ran a short sustained run yesterday against a staging instance with the config below and attached raw CSV of sample results. Highlights: 
- Model: OSS-13B-quant (int8)
- Avg payload: 256 tokens (prompt + expected response)
- Concurrency used: 18 parallel clients (steady-state)
- Sustained QPS (requests/sec): 16 RPS (steady over a 12-minute window)
- Tokens/sec (aggregate): 4,096 tps (16 * 256)
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): median 410 ms, p95 920 ms
- GPU utilization: ~63% during steady-state

Notes: We pushed batching off at the client layer (batch size 1) because of latency concerns; we did run one test with server-side batching=8 and saw tokens/sec improve to ~5,900 but p95 moved to ~1.3 s. Raw data: finova-throughput-results.csv attached.

We can commit to a 30–45 min run next Tue once you confirm the exact payloads. Also adding ops@finova to loop in infra for scheduling.

Marcus Lee
Head of AI Platform, Finova
marcus.lee@finova.com
Attachment: finova-throughput-results.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T10:35:00Z
Subject: Fwd: MAP kickoff + perf eval template (Finova results)

Forwarding Marcus’ run. Key takeaways for the MAP and pricing conversation: 
1) Sustained workload: 16 RPS at 256 tokens => 4,096 tps steady.
2) Latency: TTFT med 410 ms / p95 920 ms. That p95 is okay for their interactivity but we should aim to reduce it under 700 ms for better UX.
3) Batching tradeoff: server batching up to 8 increases throughput ~45% but tail latency increases ~40%.

Immediate asks: 
- Priyom: please draft a unit-econ view in one slide comparing (a) hosted pay-as-you-go, (b) dedicated 6-GPU pool with autoscaling, and (c) hybrid (private control plane + burst to hosted). Use our cost model assumptions (attach unit-econ-projection). Provide cost per 1M tokens, and cost per sustained RPS.
- Monica: plan a canary config for a 2-week evaluation (we want to test prefix caching and batching=4). Map milestone: 1) perf run (done), 2) canary (2w), 3) agreement for dedicated capacity.

Attaching: MAP_v2.xlsx (I’ll edit the acceptance criteria after Priyom’s econ slide).

Ben

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-23T17:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: MAP kickoff + perf eval template (Finova results) — unit econ draft

Team — quick unit-econ snapshot attached. Assumptions and outputs below (numbers rounded): 
Assumptions
- Sustained workload: 16 RPS, avg 256 tokens/request => 4,096 tokens/sec => 353.9M tokens/day => ~10.6B tokens/month (30d)
- Redwood marginal infra cost (dedicated): $0.80 per 1M tokens (GPU amortization + infra ops)
- Proposed Redwood list for dedicated tier: $1.20 per 1M tokens (tiered discounts for commitments)

Outputs (monthly)
- Cost to Redwood at $0.80/1M: 10,616 * $0.80 = $8,493 (approx)
- Revenue at $1.20/1M: 10,616 * $1.20 = $12,740
- Gross margin on tokens: ~$4,247/month (~33%)
- Per-request math: at 16 RPS, cost/request (infra) = (4,096 tps / 1,000,000)*$0.80 per sec converted -> simpler: monthly infra cost / (RPS * secs/month) => $8,493 / (16 * 2,592,000) ≈ $0.000204 per request (very small)

Config recommendations for canary (2 weeks): 
- Dedicated 6 x A100-ish equivalents, batch target = 4 (to limit p95 inflation), enable prefix/KV cache with estimated 65% hit (Finova uses many repeated prompts)
- Instrument TTFT and p95 telemetry and token accounting per route

Attachment: unit-econ-projection.xlsx

Priyom
Applied ML / Product Economics | Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finova.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T17:03:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP + perf eval — proposed close checklist and timeline

Marcus / team — thanks for the quick run and Priyom for the econ write-up. Confirming next steps and a proposed close checklist so we’re all aligned: 
1) Week of 6/1: 45-minute coordinated benchmark — we’ll run both batching=1 (latency baseline) and batching=4 (throughput baseline) for 30 minutes each. Redwood will provide a canary config (6-GPU pool) and a shared dashboard.
2) Week of 6/8–6/19: 2-week canary in your staging with telemetry turned on (TTFT, p50/p95, tokens/sec, KV cache hit). Acceptance criteria to pass into production: p95 <= 700 ms OR documented UX mitigation, sustained tokens/sec within 10% of the 6/30 test, and no regex-level data leakage flags in logs.
3) Commercial: we’ll pull together a dedicated capacity quote for 6 GPUs + 2 weeks of canary support. Target contract signature: by 2026-06-15.

Quick cost projection (monthly) based on Priyom’s numbers: ~10.6B tokens/month => Redwood list price at $1.20/1M => ~$12.7k/mo. I’ve added a 10% pilot credit in the draft quote to cover validation runs.

Marcus — if you confirm the 6/1 benchmark window, I’ll lock infra and send a short runbook.

Monica Patel | Director, Sales Ops | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: MAP_v2.xlsx (updated milestones & acceptance criteria)
